column1: # tests/ORACLES.tsv -- every oracle in tests/ and tools/, and every file that
# looks like one and is not.
# An oracle is a check against another implementation's behaviour:
# CRuby, a reference C build, a JAX or IREE reference, a replay of
# a recorded run under CRuby, a byte comparison with another implementation's
# recorded output. It runs only when the person running the suite asks for
# it, with ALLOW_ORACLE=1. A comparison within one implementation (two of its paths, or
# its old and new build) is not one, with one exception: a build by
# BASELINE_KERNEL, a kernel built without the change, compared with this one is
# an oracle. tools/oracle/gate enforces the contract.
# COLUMNS
#   path      the file, from the repository root
#   section   the name the file's gate call uses (tools/oracle/gate, or
#             OracleGate.allow? in Ruby); `whole` gates the file at its top;
#             `-` for a row that has no gate call
#   class     named       the maintainers named it an oracle; gated
#             definition  it fits the definition above; gated
#             confirm     gated until the maintainers settle whether it is an
#                         oracle
#             program     a program that performs a comparison and is run only
#                         from a gated section; no gate of its own
#             exempt      it mentions CRuby, an oracle or a replay, and is not
#                         one: the maintainers ruled so, or the comparison stays within
#                         one implementation, or the word names something else
#             ungated     an oracle this mechanism does not gate; the reason
#                         says why and who starts it
#   what      what a gated section compares with (printed by the gate), or why
#             a row is not gated
# tests/oracle/check.sh holds this list to the tree: every gate call has its
# row and every gated row its call, and every file the oracle patterns find has
# a row. Read it before adding a row.
